questions.question: The Registrar promised the judicial committee that he ___ the confidential report by Monday morning.
questions.explanation: Main clause verb 'promised' Simple Past (V2) mein hai. Past narrative context mein aage aane wale future action ke liye Future-in-the-Past ('would + V1') lagta hai. Yahan 'will' (A) tense harmony break karta hai. 'Submits' (C) aur 'has submitted' (D) present tenses hain jo past reference point ke mutabiq galat hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-04: Jab principal verb past mein ho, toh future event ke liye 'will' ki jagah 'would + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The science lecturer demonstrated to the students that water ___ at zero degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Governing verb 'demonstrated' Simple Past mein hai, lekin subordinate clause ek eternal scientific law batata hai (paani ka 0°C par freeze hona). Universal aur scientific truths past tense harmony se completely exempt hote hain aur hamesha Simple Present ('freezes') mein hi rehte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-05: Subordinate clauses jo universal truths ya scientific laws express karte hain, main verb past hone par bhi Simple Present mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: When the advocate reached the High Court premises, he realized that he ___ the case diary at his residence.
questions.explanation: Past mein do actions huye: court pahunchna aur diary chhutna. Diary chhutne ka kaam court pahunchna se pehle hua tha. Standard exam grammar mein past reference point se pehle complete huye action ke liye Past Perfect ('had left') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03: Past reference point se pehle complete huye action ke liye Past Perfect ('had + V3') use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.subtopic: Open Sequence with Present Main Verb
questions.question: The administrative officer says that the technical interview ___ tomorrow at 10:00 AM.
questions.explanation: Main verb 'says' Simple Present mein hai. Principle of Open Sequence ke mutabiq, present governing verb subordinate clause ko past mein restrict nahi karta. Interview 'tomorrow' scheduled hai, isliye standard future form 'will be conducted' sahi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-01: Jab main clause verb Present ya Future tense mein ho, toh subordinate clause mein meaning ke hisaab se koi bhi tense aa sakta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.subtopic: Purpose Clause with Past Main Verb
questions.question: The system assistant updated the security patches promptly so that the court network ___ safe from ransomware attacks.
questions.explanation: 'So that' se introduce hone wale purpose clauses mein modal auxiliary governing verb ke tense se match karta hai. Kyunki 'updated' Simple Past (V2) hai, modal strictly 'might' hona chahiye ('might remain'). 'May' aur 'can' tabhi aate hain jab main verb present ho.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-08: Past Main Verb + 'so that' / 'in order that' ke sath hamesha 'might + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The judicial magistrate observed that the petitioner ___ extremely nervous during cross-examination.
questions.explanation: Main verb 'observed' Simple Past (V2) mein hai. Petitioner ka nervous lagna aur magistrate ka observe karna past mein theek ek sath (simultaneously) hua. Isliye tense harmony ke tehat Simple Past 'looked' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-02: Past narrative mein simultaneous events ke liye Simple Past (V2) ya Past Continuous lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The legal historian explained that the Indian Constitution ___ into force on 26th January 1950.
questions.explanation: Historical events jo past ke kisi specific point par poore ho chuke hain, unke liye Simple Past ('came') lagta hai. Ye universal physical truths nahi hain, isliye inhe Simple Present ('comes') mein nahi rakha ja sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-07: Historical events ke liye Simple Past (V2) use karein; inhe universal truths se confuse na karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The senior judicial clerk respected the previous registrar more than he ___ the present administrator.
questions.explanation: 'Than' se start hone wala subordinate clause of comparison past tense harmony se completely exempt hota hai. Kyunki comparison past feeling ka 'present' administrator ke prati ongoing attitude se ho raha hai, isliye Simple Present 'respects' grammatically correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-09: 'Than' ya 'as' wale comparison clauses mein context aur logic ke hisaab se koi bhi tense aa sakta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: Find the incorrect part: The registrar informed (A) / the applicants that (B) / the final merit list (C) / will be uploaded soon. (D)
questions.explanation: Main verb 'informed' past reference frame set karta hai. Isliye part (D) ka modal auxiliary 'will' tense harmony maintain karne ke liye backshift hokar 'would' ('would be uploaded soon') banega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-04: Jab governing verb past mein ho, toh 'will' ka backshift hokar 'would' banta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The retired chief justice reminded the young probationers that slow and steady ___ the race.
questions.explanation: 'Slow and steady wins the race' ek permanent idiomatic proverb aur moral maxim hai. Reporting verb 'reminded' chahe Simple Past mein kyun na ho, proverbs hamesha Simple Present ('wins') mein hi rehte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-06: Proverbs aur moral maxims main clause ke tense ki parwah kiye bina Simple Present mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The court bailiff locked the record room securely lest unauthorized intruders ___ the sealed exhibits.
questions.explanation: Subordinating conjunction 'lest' ('kahi aisa na ho ki') ke baad strictly modal auxiliary 'should' aata hai, chahe main clause ka tense kuch bhi ho. 'May', 'might', ya 'would' wale options 'lest' ke sath grammatically invalid hote hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-08: Conjunction 'lest' ke baad hamesha 'should + V1' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02

questions.question: The High Court bench dismissed the revision petition because the appellant ___ to deposit the statutory costs on time.
questions.explanation: Cost deposit karne mein fail hona bench dwara petition dismiss karne se PEHLE hua tha. Past effect se pehle huye prior cause ke liye Past Perfect ('had failed') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule TH-03: Past main action se pehle huye cause ke liye Past Perfect ('had + V3') use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L02
